开车出发前，把没来得及读的 PDF 转给 Agent，让它念出来，接着听内容。第七期记录的这次使用，没有计时数据，但有一个很清楚的结果：人已经能听文档了，不用再操心文件如何转换。

同一期里，给录屏做包装却要等十五到二十分钟。封面、片尾、转场、目录都要做，着急发布时，自己加字幕可能还快一些。两次体验放在一起，正好说明模型响应速度解释不了整个任务的耗时。

## 先看用户什么时候能开始用

DeepSeek App 在关闭搜索时响应很快，是节目中的个人感受。要判断这种提速对产品有多大帮助，还得看输出拿来做什么。

Anthropic 的[延迟文档](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/test-and-evaluate/strengthen-guardrails/reduce-latency)把请求发出到首个 Token 返回的时间称为 TTFT。流式输出能让人提前读到开头，适合解释、问答等边读边用的内容。若任务是生成一个文件，开头几行代码出现了，用户通常还无事可做。

朗读 PDF 则有另一种安排：第一段语音准备好就开始播放，后面的内容继续处理。这是一种设计选择，节目没有说明当时的工具是否采用了这样的流水线。它值得考虑，是因为听众的使用顺序本来就是从前往后。

同样，视频导出前可以先给一段预览。预览如果足以确认字幕位置或转场样式，就能提前发现问题；只显示制作中的几行日志，对准备发视频的人帮助不大。

## 把二十分钟拆开看

用一个假设算例看得更清楚：任务共二十分钟，其中模型处理两分钟，素材传输与导出十八分钟。把模型部分缩短到十二秒，总耗时仍然是十八分十二秒。

实际排查时，需要分别记录下载、生成、渲染和上传用了多久。如果长时间停在渲染，就查输出规格、效果和执行设备；如果主要在返工，就查第一次预览为什么出现得那么晚。

包装本身也有取舍。一条临时说明功能的录屏，可能只需要裁掉空白、加上字幕。把所有动效都做齐，增加的等待未必值得。让用户选择快速版与完整包装版，往往比继续强调模型每秒输出多少 Token 更能解决眼前的问题。

## 等待时，只报告影响下一步的事

短任务马上就能结束，直接给结果即可。长任务则要让用户分辨自己该不该介入。正在导出时可以离开；源文件缺失时应当补文件；一项已经超时的外部请求，需要给出重试或取消的入口。

这类状态可以很简短，也不需要公开模型的思考过程。完成通知最好附上能直接打开的文件，避免用户回来后再问一次结果在哪。

对于 PDF 朗读，值得检查的是声音多久开始、途中会不会停、离开当前页面后还能否继续听。对于视频，检查的是预览何时可看、最终文件何时可下载。这些时间才直接关系到用户的安排。

Before setting off on a drive, send an Agent the PDF you haven’t had time to read and ask it to read it aloud, then listen to the contents. This use case, recorded in episode seven, has no timing data, but one outcome is clear: the person can listen to the document without having to worry about how to convert the file.

In the same episode, packaging a screen recording takes fifteen to twenty minutes. It needs a cover, an outro, transitions, and a table of contents. When you’re in a hurry to publish, adding subtitles yourself might be faster. Put side by side, the two experiences show why model response speed alone can’t explain how long the entire task takes.

## First, look at when users can start using the result

The feeling that the DeepSeek app responds quickly when search is turned off comes from personal experience on the show. To judge how much that speedup helps the product, you also need to consider what the output will be used for.

Anthropic’s [latency documentation](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/test-and-evaluate/strengthen-guardrails/reduce-latency) calls the time from sending a request to receiving the first token TTFT. Streaming output lets people read the beginning sooner, which works well for content they can use as they read, such as explanations and answers. If the task is to generate a file, users usually can’t do anything yet when the first few lines of code appear.

PDF narration allows for another approach: start playback as soon as the first passage of speech is ready, while the rest of the content continues to be processed. This is a design choice; the episode does not say whether the tool used at the time had such a pipeline. It is worth considering because listeners naturally use the content from beginning to end.

Similarly, you can provide a preview before a video export is complete. If the preview is enough to check subtitle placement or transition styles, it helps people spot problems early. A few lines of logs showing that work is in progress are of little use to someone preparing to publish a video.

## Break down the twenty minutes

A hypothetical example makes this clearer: the task takes twenty minutes in total, with two minutes for model processing and eighteen minutes for asset transfer and export. Shortening the model portion to twelve seconds still leaves a total time of eighteen minutes and twelve seconds.

When investigating the actual process, record separately how long downloading, generation, rendering, and uploading take. If the task spends a long time in rendering, check the output specifications, effects, and execution device. If most of the time goes to rework, find out why the first preview arrives so late.

Packaging itself involves tradeoffs, too. A screen recording made to explain a feature on the fly may only need its blank sections trimmed and subtitles added. The extra wait for completing every animation may not be worthwhile. Letting users choose between a quick version and a fully packaged version will often address their immediate problem better than continuing to emphasize how many tokens the model outputs per second.

## While users wait, report only what affects their next step

Short tasks can end quickly, so just provide the result. For longer tasks, users need to know whether they should step in. They can leave while an export is running; if a source file is missing, they should provide it; and if an external request has timed out, they need an option to retry or cancel.

These status updates can be brief and don’t need to reveal the model’s thought process. A completion notification should ideally include a file users can open directly, so they don’t have to ask where the result is when they return.

For PDF narration, check how soon the audio starts, whether it pauses along the way, and whether it can keep playing after users leave the current page. For video, check when the preview is ready and when the final file can be downloaded. These are the timings that directly affect users’ plans.

记得一位嘉宾讲过某个观点，却想不起是哪一期、哪一分钟。几百期访谈都有了文字，搜索容易一些；如果搜出的句子没有出处，还是得回到播放器里从头找。

第七期提到过一项整理尝试：获取节目官网已有字幕，缺字幕的部分再转写，整理成中文网站。转写之后，资料库还得保留能返回原材料的线索，否则内容越多，核对越费劲。

## 同一句话，可能有几层来源

发布方字幕、自行转写、中文翻译和摘要，可能都对应同一段音频。导入时应保留它们之间的关系。摘要里的判断出现问题，才知道应回查翻译、转写，还是原音频。

每条节目记录至少需要原始链接、日期、语言和文本来源。有时间码的文本，保留对应位置；没有时间码的，不要估算一个看似准确的播放时刻。

官方字幕也可能有误，只是更容易确认来源。后续若拿到修订版，应知道哪些翻译和摘要仍依据旧稿，而不是悄悄换掉原文后继续展示旧结论。

## 流畅的文字也要能回听

一个人名写成另一个熟悉的人名，读起来往往很自然。Whisper 的[模型说明](https://github.com/openai/whisper/blob/main/model-card.md)还指出，输出可能包含音频里没有说过的文字。只检查语句是否通顺，抓不到这类错误。

用于浏览的文本可以标明来源和校对情况。准备引用某句话时，则要回听相应位置，尤其留意人名、数字、否定词和限制条件。翻译也应保留原文的不确定性，不能把可能改成已经发生。

修正一个名字以后，相关翻译、摘要和搜索索引都可能需要更新。若每个段落有稳定标识，并记录派生文本引用了它，维护会比全文搜索替换可靠得多。

## 搜索时把前后条件一起带出来

假设要查某人对开源模型的看法，一段赞成，一段批评。它们可能相隔几年，也可能分别讨论个人研究与企业部署。把两句拼在一起，无法解释差别。

结果页可以先给出节目日期、话题和必要的前后文，再链接到原段落。摘要负责帮助读者决定要不要继续读；正式引用仍应落回原材料。

目录也需要显示缺失。某期没有字幕、某段转写不完整、某个视频链接失效，都应能被看见。否则一次没有搜到，很容易被误解为嘉宾从未谈过这件事。

验收时可以挑几段自己知道出处的讨论，检查能否搜到、是否定位准确、前后条件有没有丢失。再选一项资料不全的节目，确认系统会说明缺口。比起统计已经导入多少篇，这些检查更能说明资料库是否适合用来找材料。

description: 'Import episodes that already have subtitles and transcribe the rest to build up a collection quickly. To make these materials searchable and citable, you also need to preserve their sources, timestamps, missing content, and the context around each point of view.'
updatedAt: '2026-10-26'

You remember a guest making a certain point, but can’t recall which episode or minute it was. When hundreds of interviews are available as text, searching gets easier. But if the sentences you find have no source, you still have to go back to the player and search from the beginning.

The seventh episode mentioned an effort to organize this material: obtain subtitles already available on the show’s website, transcribe the episodes without them, and compile everything into a Chinese-language website. After transcription, the library still needs to retain clues that lead back to the source material. Otherwise, the more content you have, the harder it becomes to verify.

## One sentence can have several layers of sources

Publisher-provided subtitles, your own transcription, a Chinese translation, and a summary may all correspond to the same stretch of audio. When importing them, preserve the relationships between these versions. If a claim in a summary turns out to be wrong, you need to know whether to check the translation, the transcription, or the original audio.

Each episode record needs at least the original link, date, language, and text source. If a text has timestamps, preserve the corresponding positions. If it does not, don’t estimate a playback time that only looks precise.

Official subtitles can also contain errors; their source is simply easier to verify. If a revised version becomes available later, you should be able to tell which translations and summaries are still based on the old transcript, rather than quietly replacing the original and continuing to show conclusions based on it.

## Fluent text should still be checkable against the audio

One person’s name can be transcribed as another familiar name, and the result may read perfectly naturally. The [Whisper model card](https://github.com/openai/whisper/blob/main/model-card.md) also points out that the output may include words that were never spoken in the audio. Checking only whether the sentences sound smooth won’t catch this kind of error.

Text intended for browsing can be labeled with its source and proofreading status. When preparing to quote a sentence, listen to the corresponding section, paying particular attention to names, numbers, negations, and qualifying conditions. Translations should also preserve uncertainty in the original; don’t turn “might happen” into “has happened.”

After correcting a name, related translations, summaries, and search indexes may all need updating. If each passage has a stable identifier and the system records which passages derived text refers to, maintenance will be much more reliable than searching and replacing across the full text.

## Bring the surrounding conditions along in search results

Suppose you want to look up someone’s views on open-source models and find one passage in favor and another critical of them. They may be years apart, or they may discuss individual research and enterprise deployment, respectively. Putting the two sentences together does not explain the difference.

A results page can first show the episode date, topic, and necessary surrounding context, then link to the original passage. A summary helps readers decide whether to continue reading; formal citations should still point back to the source material.

The catalog also needs to show what is missing. An episode without subtitles, an incomplete transcription, or a broken video link should all be visible. Otherwise, not finding something in a search can easily be mistaken for the guest never having discussed it.

For acceptance checks, you can pick a few discussions whose sources you already know and check whether you can find them, whether they’re located accurately, and whether their surrounding conditions have been preserved. Then choose an episode with incomplete materials and confirm that the system explains the gap. These checks say more about whether the library is suitable for finding source material than a count of how many articles have been imported.

title: '给虚构角色配音，先确定他在对谁说话'
description: '用一段店主与熟客的虚构对白，讨论怎样给合成语音具体的表演要求，并检查音色一致性与对话衔接。'
updatedAt: '2026-10-26'
---

一句“欢迎回来”，放在不同场景里，读法会差很多。店主是真的高兴见到熟客，还是想装作两人并不熟？即使使用同一个声音，停顿和音量也会改变这句话的意思。

歸藏在第六期谈到把小说内容做成类似视觉小说的形式，为人物固定音色与性格。其中一个例子是年老、阴险的神父。选一个年长的声音只是起点，具体台词还得放回人物正在做的事里考虑。

## 性格标签写完以后，还缺这一句的情境

可以用一段虚构对白试试：店主认出了熟客，但不想让旁人知道两人认识。只给“神秘、复杂、富有层次”几个标签，试听时很难判断哪里应该调整。

更明确的要求可以是：开头按普通招呼读，称呼之前略停，后半句压低声音，不表现出惊讶。工具是否能准确执行，需要听生成结果；但至少能判断它有没有把熟悉关系说得太明显。

如果台词写了很长一段解释，却要求人物匆忙打断，单纯加快语速可能越听越别扭。此时应先删短对白，让人物的行动和文字长度对得上，再调整读法。

也可以保留一版自然读法，每次只换一处重音或停顿。连续试听几个版本，比不断往提示里添加性格词更容易找到想要的效果。

## 音色固定，情绪可以变化

语音合成早就有表达控制。[SSML 1.1](https://www.w3.org/TR/speech-synthesis11/)定义了发音、停顿、音高、音量和语速等标记。因此，不能把角色配音简单写成新工具有表演、旧工具只有朗读。

如今一些接口允许用自然语言描述表达方式。[Google 当前的语音生成文档](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/speech-generation)还提供声音身份和轮次风格等配置。这里可以借它了解一种制作方式，节目试用的具体模型与配置仍以节目材料为限。

声音身份与单句情绪可以分开保存：人物用哪个声音，单独固定；这句话是低声解释还是急着辩解，放在当前轮次。Google 文档也提醒，反复加入过长的角色描述可能导致声音漂移。这是该产品的使用建议，其他工具需要各自试听确认。

实际制作时，可以为人物留几段参考声音，再把后续生成与它们并排听。平静、紧张和低声说话时，是否还能认出是同一个人物？发音习惯有没有突然改变？发现变化后，回查声音配置与当前指导，比重写整份人物小传更容易定位原因。

## 两句台词，要连起来听

单句选好了，还得放回对话里。上一句结束后留了多久，下一句有没有抢话，会直接改变人物关系。原本像是不耐烦的回答，留出很长空白后，可能听成犹豫。

先把相邻两人的对白连起来，再配画面，检查称呼、读音和角色是否混淆。两个单听很好听的音色，接在一起也可能太相似。若人物在这个场景里需要被迅速认出，就要调整声音选择或说话习惯。

最后再听完整场景：店主那句压低声音的“欢迎回来”，是否被背景音乐盖掉了？熟客的下一句有没有接住这个暗示？这两处如果没成立，单句里的精细表演也很难被听众听出来。

title: '当 AI 普遍做到六十分，内容还凭什么被选择'
description: '基础质量变得容易获得之后，合格与值得阅读之间仍有距离。用创作研究区分质量提升、内容趋同与读者价值。'

一篇文章通顺，一张封面整齐，一段视频没有明显错误。过去，这些成果可能需要不少制作时间；当生成工具让它们更容易获得，完成制作本身就不再足以解释：读者为什么要选这一份？

第 006 期提到一个尖锐的判断：只要 AI 把一个东西拉到六十分，那六十分就是零分。把它当成分数结论显然不准确。六十分的结果仍可能帮助一个人解决问题；值得讨论的，是当合格作品变多之后，基础制作质量还能带来多少选择优势。

## 可用价值与选择优势不同

一份只供自己看的整理笔记，结构清楚、信息够用，可能已经完成任务。它不需要比别人的笔记更独特，也不需要吸引陌生人停留。若生成工具降低了整理成本，这份结果的价值并不会因为别人也能做到而消失。

公开发布的内容面对另一种约束。读者可以跳过，可以选择相近主题的其他文章，也可以直接向模型提问。一份作品达到可读标准之后，还需要给读者一个选择它的理由。

因此，六十分变零分更适合被理解为竞争位置的变化，而非使用价值归零。把两者混在一起，会误伤许多有用的日常自动化，也会让公开创作把精力耗在无止境的装饰上。

## 质量提高，作品仍可能更相像

Anil R. Doshi 与 Oliver P. Hauser 的一项在线故事写作实验，观察了使用生成式 AI 提供故事点子的影响。研究发现，获得 AI 点子的作品在写作与阅读体验评价上有所提升，但这些作品彼此之间也更相似。研究对象是特定的故事创作任务，不能直接据此推断所有文章、图片或视频都会趋同。

它提供的启发是，单篇质量与一批作品的差异程度可以同时朝不同方向变化。每个人都获得了更容易使用的起点，并不保证最终集合里的选择更丰富。[论文原文](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.00506)支持这一实验范围内的判断，并没有给出一个适用于所有内容的六十分阈值。

放到编辑工作中，一个值得检查的现象是：几篇稿件分别读都完整，放在同一个列表里，却在解释同一种泛泛的问题，使用相近的结构，得出几乎相同的建议。逐篇润色可以改善句子，未必能解决选题之间缺少差异的问题。

## 差异可以来自更具体的材料

假设两篇文章都在讨论 Agent 能否提高效率。一篇列出常见好处，另一篇记录某个剪辑任务实际交付了什么、遗漏了什么，以及发现遗漏的方法。后者不必使用更夸张的标题，就已经提供了不同的信息。

差异来自问题和材料的选择。一个清楚的失败案例、一组可复查的条件、对适用边界的解释，都可以让读者知道哪些判断与自己有关。它们不能靠更换形容词补出来，也不一定需要更长的文章。

这种材料可以由人搜集，也可以由 Agent 帮助检索、整理和核对。重要的是它是否真实存在，来源能否支撑相应说法。仅仅把通用内容改写得更像个人口吻，并不会自动获得这些信息。

## 包装服务于读者要完成的事

提高制作质量仍然有价值。字幕清楚可以降低理解成本，图表可以展示文字不容易比较的差别，结构合理可以帮助读者找到所需信息。它们的价值来自具体用途，而非单纯比上一版更复杂。

同样，增加一段配音、一组转场或一个视频版本，也应回答它帮助谁解决了什么问题。对需要快速查找信息的人，更多播放时长可能增加负担；对需要观察操作过程的人，视频又可能比文字更合适。

这给创作留下一个比追逐固定分数更稳定的判断方式：保留基础质量，再检查作品是否带来了足够具体的信息，是否让目标读者更容易理解或行动。工具越容易做出合格的外观，选择问题、寻找材料与判断用途的工作就越需要认真完成。

An article reads smoothly, a cover looks polished, a video has no obvious errors. In the past, producing these results might have taken considerable time. Now that generative tools make them easier to achieve, completing the production itself is no longer enough to explain why readers should choose this piece.

Episode 006 raised a pointed claim: once AI brings something up to 60 points, those 60 points are worth zero. Clearly, that is not an accurate conclusion about the score itself. A result worth 60 points may still help someone solve a problem. What is worth discussing is how much of a competitive advantage basic production quality can still provide once more work meets the bar.

## Usefulness and a competitive edge are different

A set of organized notes intended only for personal use may have done its job if it is clear and contains enough information. It does not need to be more distinctive than someone else’s notes or make strangers stop and read. If generative tools lower the cost of organizing information, the result does not lose its value just because others can do the same.

Public content faces a different constraint. Readers can skip it, choose another article on a similar topic, or ask a model directly. Once a piece is readable, it still needs to give readers a reason to choose it.

So “60 becomes zero” is better understood as a shift in competitive position, not a loss of all practical value. Confusing the two would undervalue many useful everyday automations and lead public creators to spend their energy on endless embellishment.

## Quality can improve while works become more alike

An online storytelling experiment by Anil R. Doshi and Oliver P. Hauser examined the effects of using generative AI to provide story ideas. The study found that works created with AI ideas received higher ratings for writing and reading experience, while also becoming more similar to one another. The study focused on a specific storytelling task, so its findings cannot be used to conclude directly that all articles, images, or videos will converge.

One takeaway is that the quality of individual pieces and the diversity of a collection can move in different directions at the same time. Giving everyone an easier starting point does not guarantee more variety in the final selection. The [original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.00506) supports conclusions within the scope of this experiment; it does not establish a 60-point threshold that applies to all content.

In editorial work, one pattern worth checking is this: several drafts each feel complete on their own, but when placed in the same list, they explain the same broad problem, use similar structures, and reach almost identical recommendations. Polishing each draft may improve the sentences without solving the lack of distinction between the topics.

## Difference can come from more specific material

Suppose two articles both discuss whether Agents can improve efficiency. One lists common benefits; the other documents what a particular editing task actually delivered, what it missed, and how those omissions were discovered. The latter already provides different information without needing a more sensational headline.

Difference comes from the choice of question and material. A clear failure case, a set of verifiable conditions, or an explanation of where something applies can help readers see which judgments are relevant to them. These things cannot be supplied by swapping in different adjectives, and they do not necessarily require a longer article.

People can gather this material, or Agents can help retrieve, organize, and verify it. What matters is whether the material actually exists and whether its sources support the claims being made. Merely rewriting generic content to sound more personal does not automatically add this information.

## Packaging should serve what readers need to do

Improving production quality still matters. Clear subtitles can reduce the effort needed to understand something, charts can show differences that are hard to compare in text, and a sound structure can help readers find the information they need. Their value comes from a specific use, not simply from being more elaborate than the previous version.

Likewise, adding a voice-over, transitions, or a video version should answer what problem it helps someone solve. For people who need to find information quickly, more playback time may add a burden. For those who need to observe a process, video may be more suitable than text.

This leaves creators with a more stable way to judge their work than chasing a fixed score: maintain basic quality, then check whether the work offers sufficiently specific information and helps its intended readers understand or act more easily. The easier tools make it to achieve a competent appearance, the more carefully creators need to choose questions, find material, and judge what it is for.

The launcher redesign in episode seven starts here: take inspiration from existing projects and adapt a home screen to your own habits.

## Try it with the remote first

On a phone, you can tap directly. TVs often rely on the directional pad to move focus from item to item. Where frequently used apps are placed, which one is selected by default, and where the Back button takes you all have more impact on usability than how many cards fit on the screen.

Android’s [TV navigation guide](https://developer.android.com/training/tv/get-started/navigation) emphasizes short navigation paths and using the directional pad to reach every visible control. To check yours, start from power-on, go all the way to playing content, then return to the home screen. If even one dialog along the way cannot be closed with the remote, the path is not complete.

You can start by putting only frequently used shortcuts on the home screen. If you need search, recently watched content, or other features, see whether adding them pushes the original buttons farther away. Try each new shortcut with the remote again.

## Check issues with the old device separately

The episode also features a TV that often reports low memory, even though not many apps have been added. This description alone is not enough to determine the cause, and it is unclear whether the warning refers to RAM or storage space.

Changing the launcher can change the home screen, but it may not solve this kind of problem. If an app will not open, playback stutters, or the system reports insufficient space, check the corresponding error and the device status. A home screen that feels snappier cannot replace those checks.

It is also useful to keep the original recovery path before making changes. If the new home screen has a problem, being able to return to settings or the original launcher means a UI experiment will not get in the way of everyday TV use.

A separate TV entry point that shows only selected tasks would be easier to manage than copying the entire desktop.

做游戏时用了 AI，玩家运行游戏时未必还要调用模型。一段生成好的程序，可以像其他程序一样处理移动、碰撞和升级。模型参与过制作，并不会让每次按键都产生 Token 费用。

第七期聊到 PokéBonk，使用感受集中在几个细节：手机和电脑都能打开，再次进入时进度还在。节目没有提供它的完整技术栈或经核实的经营数据。可以从这些体验谈网页游戏的完成度，不能替开发者断言它到底怎样使用 AI。

## 哪些内容在制作时确定，哪些需要现场生成

假设做一个打怪升级游戏。地图、敌人行为、掉落规则和装备说明，都可以在开发时生成并写进程序。玩家重复游玩，执行的是已经交付的代码。

若希望每个 NPC 都能针对玩家的自由输入作答，模型就进入了运行环节。此时要考虑一次对话的等待、调用失败的处理，以及玩家人数增加后的费用。也可以只让少数角色具备这项能力，其他部分沿用固定规则。

选择时可以拿一段玩法具体比较：预先写好的分支是否已经够用？自由生成是否带来玩家能够感受到的变化？如果只是在相同意思上换几种措辞，在线生成增加的费用和不稳定性可能不划算。

## 初始投入可以分摊，服务费用仍会发生

一个假设的单人浏览器游戏，初始制作成本是 C，累计有 N 次游玩。只分摊这笔制作成本，每次是 C/N。这个算式没有计入资源下载、服务器和后续维护。

账号、排行榜、联机状态以及支付，都可能带来持续开销。运行时使用模型的部分，还要另算调用成本。讨论低成本分发时，需要先说明游戏究竟把哪些计算留给客户端，哪些仍依赖服务端。

节目提出的做法是把制作阶段的投入变成能够被反复使用的作品。这种成本结构值得尝试，但收入还取决于玩家是否愿意付费，以及获客、更新和运营要花多少钱。

## 一个链接能打开，手机上是否真的好玩

[MDN 的网页游戏发布指南](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Games/Publishing_games)介绍了自行托管和市场分发等路径。网页方便通过链接试用，适合把一个小版本尽早交给别人玩。

这些问题在桌面演示里很容易漏掉。[浏览器的图形、输入、音频和存储能力](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Games/Introduction)提供了开发基础，实际体验还要由游戏处理。

早期版本可以只做一段完整流程：进入、游玩、失败或结束、退出，再次打开。把这段流程交给朋友，观察他在哪儿卡住，比先堆更多关卡更容易发现问题。等他愿意主动再玩一局，再考虑增加内容和付费设计。

title: 'Two Costs of AI Games: Production and Operation'
description: 'Generated code can be run repeatedly, while dialogue generated in real time keeps incurring call costs. When making a browser game, how should you choose and estimate these two kinds of investment?'
updatedAt: '2026-10-26'

Using AI to make a game does not necessarily mean players have to call a model when they play it. Generated code can handle movement, collisions, and upgrades just like any other program. The fact that a model helped make the game does not mean every button press incurs a Token cost.

Episode 7 discussed PokéBonk, with impressions focused on a few details: it can be opened on both phones and computers, and progress is still there when you return. The episode did not provide its complete tech stack or verified business data. These experiences can be a starting point for discussing how polished browser games are, but they do not let us claim on the developer's behalf exactly how it uses AI.

## What is decided during production, and what needs to be generated live

Suppose you are making a monster-fighting and leveling game. The map, enemy behavior, drop rules, and equipment descriptions can all be generated during development and written into the program. When players replay the game, they are running code that has already been delivered.

If you want every NPC to respond to players' free-form input, the model becomes part of the live operation. You then need to consider the wait for each conversation, how to handle failed calls, and the costs as the number of players grows. You could also give this capability to only a few characters and use fixed rules for everything else.

To make a choice, compare a specific section of gameplay: are prewritten branches already enough? Does free-form generation create a difference players can feel? If it only rephrases the same meaning in a few ways, the extra cost and instability of live generation may not be worthwhile.

## Initial investment can be spread out, but service costs still arise

For a hypothetical single-player browser game with an initial production cost of C and a cumulative N plays, the production cost allocated per play is C/N. This calculation does not include resource downloads, servers, or ongoing maintenance.

Accounts, leaderboards, multiplayer state, and payments may all bring ongoing costs. Any part that uses a model at runtime also has call costs to account for separately. When discussing low-cost distribution, first explain which computations the game leaves to the client and which still depend on the server.

The approach proposed in the episode is to turn production-stage investment into a work that can be used repeatedly. This cost structure is worth trying, but revenue still depends on whether players are willing to pay, as well as how much it costs to acquire players, update the game, and operate it.

## A link opens, but is it really fun on a phone?

[MDN's guide to publishing web games](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Games/Publishing_games) describes options such as self-hosting and distribution through marketplaces. Web games are easy to try through a link, making it practical to get an early version into other people's hands.

Compatibility still needs to be checked on devices. A small button that is easy to click precisely with a mouse may be hard to use on a touchscreen. If keyboard movement is replaced with a virtual joystick, how much of the screen will it cover? Does the game resume after the page goes into the background and returns? If progress is saved in the current browser, can players continue on another device?

These issues are easy to miss in a desktop demo. [Browsers' graphics, input, audio, and storage capabilities](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Games/Introduction) provide the foundation for development; the game itself still has to handle the actual experience.

An early version can include just one complete flow: enter, play, fail or finish, exit, and open it again. Handing that flow to a friend and watching where they get stuck makes problems easier to spot than adding more levels first. Once they want to play another round on their own, consider adding content and payment options.

description: '体测取消以后，旧日程和准备提醒怎么办？从一次学校邮件提醒出发，讨论活动关联、变更记录与重复通知。'

出门前收到一条提醒：北京次日有大雨，学校邮件通知体测取消。这是杨攀在第六期分享的一次 Dots 使用经历；他同样接入了 Grok Bot，但那次没有收到后者的提醒。

这段经历停在“及时告知”。节目没有说助手随后改了日历，也没有说它处理了家里全部准备事项。不过，顺着这封邮件往下想，会遇到一个很实际的问题：原来那项活动还留在日历里，旧提醒怎么办？

## 后来的通知，要接回原来的活动

假设学校先发运动会通知，几天后调整场地，前一天又因天气取消。把三封邮件各建成一项日程，家长就得自己辨认哪条有效。直接保留最新邮件也不够，因为里面可能只有一句“原定活动取消”，没有重写时间和活动名称。

助手需要把后来的通知接回原活动。邮件线程可以提供线索，学校、班级、活动名和原日期也可以用来核对；遇到同一天两个班都有相似活动，就不能只按标题匹配。

相对日期尤其容易错。周一发出的“明天”，到周二转发时仍指周二，不能因为今天才读到，就再向后推一天。要保留原通知的发送时间，并分清转发者有没有添加新的说明。

日历协议已经有一套表达这类关系的字段。[RFC 5545](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5545.html)用 UID 标识同一组件，用 SEQUENCE 表示修订序号，事件还可以标记为 CANCELLED。学校普通邮件未必带这些字段，但设计活动记录时可以参照这种方式：同一件事有稳定标识，变更附到原记录上。

## 取消体测，不等于明天不用上学

更新记录时，最容易过头的地方是替通知补全后果。取消体测，只支持取消这一项活动；是否照常到校、是否延期、是否还要携带装备，要看通知实际写了什么。只说“另行安排”，日历就应保留日期未定，不能填一个看起来合理的下周时间。

如果原来设置过“今晚准备体测装备”的提醒，可以把它与体测活动关联。活动取消后，这条提醒也会被找出来处理。若助手只有读取权限，则应显示待更新的旧安排；已有修改权限的，修改后给出结果和原邮件入口，便于家长核对。

产品也可以把一次变化显示得很短：原定日期、取消的项目、通知时间，加上原文链接。家长最需要确认的是变化影响到了哪里，无须再读一段泛泛的天气摘要。

检验这个功能时，可以按顺序输入四封虚构通知：宣布活动、换场地、重复转发、取消活动。结束后应只剩一条活动记录，能查到场地变过一次，状态为取消，旧准备提醒也有明确去向。再加一封同名但属于另一个班的通知，检查它是否被错误合并。

A reminder arrives before heading out: heavy rain is forecast for Beijing the next day, and an email from the school says fitness testing has been canceled. This is an experience Yang Pan shared in episode 6 about using Dots; he had also connected Grok Bot, but did not receive a reminder from it that time.

The account ends with “being notified in time.” The episode does not say that the assistant then updated the calendar, or that it handled all the preparations at home. Still, following the email to its practical next question: the original event is still on the calendar. What should happen to the old reminder?

## Later notices need to reconnect to the original event

Suppose the school first announces a sports day, changes the venue a few days later, then cancels it the day before because of the weather. If each of the three emails becomes a separate calendar event, parents have to figure out for themselves which one is current. Simply keeping the latest email is not enough either: it may say only “the previously scheduled event is canceled,” without restating the time or event name.

The assistant needs to link later notices back to the original event. The email thread can offer clues, as can the school, class, event name, and original date. If two classes have similar events on the same day, matching by title alone is not enough.

Relative dates are especially easy to get wrong. If an email sent on Monday says “tomorrow,” it still means Tuesday when forwarded on Tuesday; it must not be pushed back another day just because that is when it was read. The original notice’s send time needs to be preserved, and the system needs to distinguish whether the person forwarding it added any new information.

Calendar protocols already have fields for expressing these relationships. [RFC 5545](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5545.html) uses a UID to identify the same component and SEQUENCE to indicate its revision number; an event can also be marked CANCELLED. Ordinary school emails may not include these fields, but activity records can follow the same approach: give the same event a stable identifier and attach changes to its original record.

## Canceling fitness testing doesn’t mean there’s no school tomorrow

The easiest place to go too far when updating a record is to infer consequences that the notice doesn’t state. Canceling fitness testing supports canceling that event only. Whether students should still come to school as usual, whether it will be rescheduled, and whether they still need to bring their gear all depend on what the notice actually says. If there was already a reminder to “prepare fitness testing gear tonight,” it can be linked to the fitness testing event. When the event is canceled, that reminder can be found and handled too. If the assistant has read-only access, it should show the old plan as pending an update. If it already has permission to make changes, it can update the plan and show the result along with a link to the original email so parents can check it.

The product could display a change in just a few details: the originally scheduled date, the canceled item, the notice time, and a link to the original. What parents most need to confirm is what the change affects; they don’t need to read another generic weather summary.

To test this feature, enter four fictional notices in order: announce the event, change the venue, forward the notice again, and cancel the event. At the end, there should be just one event record, showing that the venue changed once, that the event is canceled, and where the old preparation reminder went. description: '任务开始后才发现更合适的方向，是协作中的常态。怎样让中途补充的要求真正改变执行，并避免旧结果覆盖新决定？'

页面正在生成，用户发现标题需要修改；图片还没做好，又决定换成竖版。工作进行到一半才想清楚要求，很正常。若每次都等整项任务结束，已经知道要改的部分还会继续白做。

第七期提到，原先习惯等 Agent 完成再提要求，后来开始直接在执行中补充。输入框可以继续使用以后，还要确认新要求究竟影响了哪些工作。

## 同一句补充，可能影响不同范围

假设 Agent 正在制作三张海报。补一个地址，通常只影响文字；横版改竖版，会影响整套布局；停下来，则需要阻止后续操作。

有些步骤尚未开始，调整计划即可。有些图片已经交给外部工具生成，未必能立即取消。产品应把这一区别告诉用户：哪部分已改，哪部分还在等待，哪些结果会作废。

Temporal 的[工作流消息文档](https://docs.temporal.io/encyclopedia/workflow-message-passing)提供了一个技术参照：Query 读取状态，Signal 异步修改，Update 允许等待处理结果或错误。节目中的产品未必使用这套实现，但它说明收到消息与处理完成可以分别表示。

面向用户的反馈不需要照搬术语。说明前两张需要重做、第三张将使用新尺寸，已经足够让人知道修改有没有落到实际任务上。

## 旧结果晚到，最容易覆盖新决定

继续用海报作例子。横版图先提交生成，用户随后改成竖版。竖版先返回，旧横版几分钟后才到。如果系统把最后收到的文件当成最终文件，已经修好的尺寸就会倒退。

给每次请求保留所依据的要求版本，可以避免这种混淆。旧图可以留下供查看，但交付位置应指向当前要求对应的结果。若标题修改了三次，也不应让第一次生成的图片重新进入成品包。

这个问题也会出现在验证环节。代码修改后，之前的测试结果不能证明新代码通过；报表筛选条件变了，旧表格就需要重新计算。新指令影响哪些产物和检查，应一起处理。

## 给用户一个能确认的当前状态

多次修改之后，可以在成品旁边保留一小段当前要求：竖版、使用哪个标题、哪些图片已经更新。用户有疑问时可以直接对照，不必翻回十几条聊天记录。

状态只需在关键变化时更新。若两个要求冲突，就问清冲突的部分；能继续做的工作不必全部停下。外部操作无法中断时，应说明它还会产生什么结果，以及该结果会被怎样处理。

最终交付前，再按当前要求检查一次文件。用户想看到的是这次修改已经体现在海报里；一句已收到，还不足以让他放心关掉窗口。

A page is being generated when the user realizes the title needs changing; the images are not ready yet when they decide to switch to portrait format. It is normal to clarify requirements halfway through the work. If every time we wait until the entire task is finished, the parts we already know need changing will keep being done in vain.

The seventh episode mentioned that people used to wait until an Agent finished before making requests, but later began adding them directly during execution. Once the input box can remain in use, we still need to confirm exactly which work the new requirements affect.

## The same addition can affect different scopes

Suppose an Agent is making three posters. Adding an address usually affects only the text; changing landscape to portrait affects the whole layout; stopping requires preventing subsequent actions.

Some steps have not started yet, so the plan can simply be adjusted. Some images have already been handed off to an external tool for generation and may not be cancellable right away. The product should tell users the difference: what has changed, what is still pending, and which results will be discarded.

Temporal's [workflow message documentation](https://docs.temporal.io/encyclopedia/workflow-message-passing) offers a technical point of reference: a Query reads state, a Signal changes it asynchronously, and an Update allows waiting for a result or an error. The product discussed in the episode may not use this implementation, but it shows that receiving a message and finishing its processing can be represented separately.

User-facing feedback does not need to copy the terminology. Explaining that the first two posters need to be redone and the third will use the new dimensions is enough to let people know whether the change has been applied to the actual task.

## Late-arriving old results can most easily override new decisions

Take the posters again as an example. A landscape image is submitted for generation, and then the user switches to portrait. The portrait version comes back first, and the old landscape version arrives a few minutes later. If the system treats the last file received as the final one, the dimensions that were already fixed will revert.

Keeping the version of the requirements each request was based on can prevent this confusion. The old image can remain available for viewing, but the delivery location should point to the result that matches the current requirements. If the title has been changed three times, the image generated for the first title should not re-enter the final package.

This issue can also arise during validation. Test results from before a code change cannot prove that the new code passes; if report filters change, the old table needs to be recalculated. The new instruction's effects on deliverables and checks should be handled together.

## Give users a current status they can verify

After multiple changes, a short summary of the current requirements can be kept beside the deliverables: portrait format, which title to use, and which images have been updated. If users have questions, they can compare directly without searching through a dozen chat messages.

Update the status only when something important changes. If two requirements conflict, clarify the conflicting part; there is no need to stop all the work that can continue. When an external operation cannot be interrupted, explain what result it will still produce and how that result will be handled.

Before final delivery, check the files once more against the current requirements. Users want to see that this change has been reflected in the poster; a simple “received” is not enough to reassure them that they can close the window.

title: '整理几百本书，是假提效，还是收纳的快乐？'
description: '一次微信读书书架整理，引出了对个人 Agent 价值的分歧。省时间、重新找到内容和单纯享受秩序，应该分别衡量。'
updatedAt: '2026-10-19'
publishedAt: '2026-10-19'
---

几百本书已经加入微信读书书架，却一直没有认真分组。一次整理把书目拉到本地，让 Agent 提出分类，由用户确认后，再通过 Computer Use 操作 Mac 上的应用，把书一本本放回相应分组。按这次使用记录，一个多小时后，书架整理完成。

这件事很快引出争论：排好之后会怎么看？如果并没有因此多读一本书，算不算假提效？另一种理解则简单得多——这就是一次收纳。

两个判断看似冲突，其实在衡量不同的结果。一个要求整理带来后续产出，另一个把恢复秩序本身当作想完成的事。

## 先分清这一小时换来了什么

这次任务明确完成的是分类与归位。它没有提供整理前后的找书时间，也没有记录后续阅读量，更没有证明省下了多少人工小时。把一个多小时的执行时间写成节省一个多小时，会偷换比较对象：如果用户原本不会亲自整理，就不存在同等长度的人工工作被替代。

但原本不会做，不代表不值得做。很多个人事务长期搁置，并非毫无意义，只是它们的价值不足以抵消当时的执行成本。工具降低成本后，重新整理书架、把收藏汇总成清单，都可能进入愿意尝试的范围。

这里新增的价值，是以前没有得到的结果。它可以有用，也可以只是让人满意；两者都需要与成本比较，却不必被强行换算成工作效率。

## 分类应该贴近下一次使用

书架可以按学科、作者、阅读进度分类，也可以按当前正在研究的问题分类。这些方式没有脱离用途的优劣。一个准备写文章的人，与一个想找周末读物的人，可能需要完全不同的入口。

个人信息管理研究长期关注的，正是已经保存的东西如何回到日常活动里。William Jones 在 Keeping Found Things Found 项目的介绍中，把有效的信息管理与日常规划联系起来。这个视角提供了一种提醒：分类系统的意义可以从未来要做的事情反推，而不只是追求目录看起来整齐。

假设某人正在研究城市生活，一本建筑史和一本小说可能值得放在同一组；若严格按出版分类分开，反而增加来回寻找的步骤。反过来，如果用途只是浏览全部藏书，一个稳定、简单的学科分类也可能足够。

Agent 可以降低提出分类方案的成本，用户仍然需要认得这些类别。一个机器解释得很完整、自己下次却想不起来的体系，很难成为长期入口。

## 收纳有终点，整理也可能成为拖延

把收纳的愉悦承认为价值，并不意味着所有整理都值得继续。分类刚完成，又想统一封面、补齐简介、打上多层标签，接着做阅读计划，一项原本有限的任务可以不断扩张。

若目标就是把混乱书架整理到看着舒服，达到这个状态便可以结束。若目标是更方便阅读，则值得回到真正的使用：需要一本书时能不能找到，刚买的书能不能轻松归位，分类是否还需要经常重做。

这些问题可以在后续使用中回答，无需为了证明提效再建一套复杂仪表盘。挑几个真实的找书场景观察，就比统计新增了多少标签更接近目标。

一次整理若只是带来满足感，也可以如实把它称为整理。真正需要警惕的，是不断扩大的准备工作挤占了原本想做的事，却始终用效率来解释。

## 个人 Agent 不必只做能写进周报的事

商业工具常用节省工时和增加收入解释价值。个人生活里还有兴趣、舒适、秩序感与探索，它们未必对应产出指标。花时间做一张个人书单，与花时间摆放实体书一样，可以由使用者自己的偏好决定。

不过，这种价值也不能替产品免去检验。一次让人开心的整理，是否足以支撑长期订阅，是另一回事；分类完成的瞬间好看，也不能证明此后仍有用。单次满足和持续使用应分别观察。

对这次书架整理，最准确的结论仍然具体：用户完成了一项想做的收纳工作，后续阅读收益尚未被记录。个人 Agent 的价值可以从这里开始，无需先把每一种生活愿望包装成生产力。

description: 'An organizing session on a WeChat Read bookshelf sparked disagreement about the value of personal agents. Saving time, finding content again, and simply enjoying order should be measured separately.'

Hundreds of books had been added to a WeChat Read bookshelf, but never properly sorted into groups. In one organizing session, the book list was brought to a local device, an Agent proposed categories, and the user confirmed them. Then, using Computer Use, the Agent operated the app on a Mac and moved the books one by one into their corresponding groups. According to the record of this session, the bookshelf was organized in a little over an hour.

The task soon prompted a debate: How would the books be used once sorted? If it did not lead to reading even one more book, was it false productivity? Another interpretation was much simpler: this was just tidying up.

These two judgments may seem to conflict, but they measure different outcomes. One requires organizing to lead to later output; the other treats restoring order as the task itself.

## First, separate what that hour accomplished

What this task clearly completed was categorizing and putting the books away. It did not provide book-finding times before and after, record subsequent reading, or establish how many hours of manual work it saved. Calling a little over an hour of execution “a little over an hour saved” would change what is being compared: if the user would not have organized the books by hand in the first place, there was no equivalent amount of manual work being replaced.

But the fact that someone would not have done something before does not mean it is not worth doing. Many personal tasks are put off for a long time, not because they are meaningless, but because their value is not enough to outweigh the effort required at the time. When tools lower that cost, reorganizing a bookshelf or turning saved items into a list may become worth trying.

The value added here is an outcome that had not been achieved before. It may be useful, or it may simply be satisfying. Either way, it should be weighed against the cost, but there is no need to force it into a measure of work efficiency.

## Categories should support the next use

A bookshelf can be organized by discipline, author, or reading progress, or by the question someone is currently researching. None of these approaches is better apart from its purpose. Someone preparing to write an article may need a very different way in than someone looking for a weekend read.

Research on personal information management has long focused on how things that have been saved can be brought back into everyday activities. In introducing the Keeping Found Things Found project, William Jones connected effective information management with everyday planning. This perspective offers a useful reminder: a system of categories can be designed backward from what someone plans to do in the future, rather than simply aiming for a tidy-looking directory.

Suppose someone is researching urban life. A history of architecture and a novel might belong in the same group; separating them strictly by publication category could instead add steps to finding them. Conversely, if the purpose is simply to browse the whole collection, a stable, simple classification by discipline may be enough.

An Agent can lower the cost of proposing a categorization scheme, but the user still needs to recognize the categories. A system that a machine can explain in full, but that the user cannot remember the next time around, is unlikely to serve as a lasting point of entry.

## Tidying has an endpoint; organizing can also become procrastination

Recognizing the pleasure of tidying as a value does not mean every organizing task is worth continuing. Once the categories are in place, someone may want to standardize the covers, fill in missing descriptions, add multiple layers of tags, and then make a reading plan. A task that started out with a clear limit can keep expanding.

If the goal is to get the messy bookshelf into a state that feels good to look at, the task can end when it reaches that state. If the goal is to make reading more convenient, it is worth returning to actual use: Can someone find a book when they need it? Can a newly purchased book be put away easily? Do the categories still need frequent reworking?

These questions can be answered through later use; there is no need to build a complicated dashboard to prove productivity. Observing a few real book-finding situations is closer to the goal than counting how many new tags were added.

If an organizing session brings only a sense of satisfaction, it can simply be called organizing. The real concern is when ever-expanding preparation takes time away from what someone originally wanted to do, while efficiency remains the explanation for it.

## Personal agents do not have to do only things that fit in a weekly report

Commercial tools often explain their value in terms of hours saved and revenue gained. Personal life also includes interests, comfort, a sense of order, and exploration, which may not correspond to output metrics. Spending time making a personal book list, like spending time arranging physical books, can be guided by the user's own preferences.

Still, that value does not exempt a product from evaluation. Whether one enjoyable organizing session is enough to justify a long-term subscription is a separate question; nor does a categorization looking good at the moment it is completed prove it will remain useful. One-time satisfaction and continued use should be observed separately.

For this bookshelf-organizing session, the most accurate conclusion remains specific: the user completed an organizing task they wanted to do, and any benefits to subsequent reading have not yet been recorded. The value of a personal Agent can begin here, without first packaging every kind of personal wish as productivity.

description: '一份聊天摘要的价值，可以落在重新打开某条讨论上。从限定检索范围到补齐后续回复，怎样让 Agent 帮人回到值得继续的工作？'

产品讨论频道里，几条建议没有及时看，过了一周就沉到历史消息里。偶尔想起来，只记得讨论过某个功能，已经不知道该搜谁、搜哪个词。

第七期的一次使用中，Agent 回看了最近一个月的 Slack 产品讨论，整理出提议与参与情况。橘子由此发现漏看的想法，接着让它给出消息链接，再回去补读。这个结果很具体：找回了值得读的几段讨论。

## 检索范围要跟着问题走

如果想找产品建议，可以限定频道、日期和议题。Slack 的搜索支持 `in:`、日期修饰符和 `is:thread` 等条件，[官方文档](https://slack.com/help/articles/202528808-Search-in-Slack-)列出了用法。

Agent 可以帮助组织检索词，但结果里仍要说明查过哪里。只读一个频道，就可能漏掉其他频道的后续决定；只读主消息，没有展开回复，也无法判断建议是否已有人处理。

与其一次要求总结整个工作区，不如先找一个具体问题：最近一个月，有没有关于注册流程、尚未得到明确回应的建议？结果容易人工抽查，漏掉什么也更容易发现。

## 读到后面，建议可能已经有了结论

假设月初有人提议缩短注册表单。后面的线程中，有人补充了必要字段的原因，最终决定先修改帮助文案。如果只摘出第一条建议，读者很可能再次发起已经结束的讨论。

每条推荐可以附上简短的当前状态：提出了什么，后续是否有结论，为什么还值得看。没有找到结论时，就写没有找到，不从沉默推断大家同意了。

链接最好直接到消息或线程。回到频道首页后还要重新搜索，会抵消摘要省下的时间。涉及多个时间段的讨论，也应分别保留出处，避免把一次旧结论套到新的条件上。

## 计数适合找线索，不适合评价一个人

节目中的任务统计了谁提出想法、谁参加讨论。这样的表可以帮助找到联系人，却很难用于比较贡献。连续五条补充可能只表达一个意见，一条指出关键限制的回复则可能改变整个方案。

A few suggestions in the product discussion channel went unread, then sank into the message history over the course of a week. When someone occasionally remembered them, they could recall that a certain feature had been discussed, but no longer knew whom to search for or which words to search.

## Let the search scope follow the question

If you want to find product suggestions, you can narrow the search by channel, date, and topic. Slack search supports conditions such as `in:`, date modifiers, and `is:thread`; the [official documentation](https://slack.com/help/articles/202528808-Search-in-Slack-) lists how to use them.

An Agent can help organize search terms, but the results should still say where it looked. Reading only one channel could miss later decisions in other channels; reading only the main message without expanding the replies makes it impossible to tell whether someone has already handled the suggestion.

Rather than asking for a summary of the entire workspace at once, start with a specific question: In the past month, were there any suggestions about the registration flow that have not received a clear response? The results are easy to spot-check manually, and it is easier to notice what might have been missed.

## By the time you read on, a suggestion may already have a conclusion

Suppose someone suggested shortening the registration form at the beginning of the month. Later in the thread, someone explained why certain fields were necessary, and the final decision was to revise the help copy first. If only the initial suggestion is excerpted, a reader could easily restart a discussion that has already concluded.

Each recommendation can include a brief status: what was proposed, whether there was a later conclusion, and why it is still worth reading. If no conclusion was found, say so; do not infer from silence that everyone agreed.

Links should point directly to the message or thread. Having to search again after returning to the channel homepage would cancel out the time saved by the summary. Discussions spanning multiple periods should also keep their sources separate, to avoid applying an old conclusion to new conditions.

The task in the episode counted who proposed ideas and who joined discussions. A table like this can help find the right contacts, but it is difficult to use for comparing contributions. Design drafts, code, and in-person discussions may not be within the search scope either. Ranking people by work visible in chat leaves out a great deal of information. If the goal is simply to catch up, sorting by topic and current status is enough.

description: '通用能力、个人偏好、项目资源和执行方法被装进同一个 Skill。模型升级之后，哪些内容值得保留，哪些应该重新验证？'

publishedAt: '2026-10-19'

一句话已经能让模型做出视频，还需要安装一套剪辑 Skill 吗？如果要求只是有画面、有声音，也许很快就能得到一个结果。但想沿用自己的字幕、素材、节奏和发布规格，问题就具体得多。

一次 AI 早报制作的分享，呈现了另一种复杂度：用户给出一段提示词，让 Bot 安装四五个已有 Skill，再调用它们完成任务。原本为了省去重复说明而建立的封装，逐渐又需要一层说明才能被使用。Prompt 和 Skill 的边界变得模糊，但用户希望保留下来的东西未必相同。

## 模型会做，和知道你要什么，隔着一层信息

可以把一套剪辑 Skill 想象成几个不同部分。如何切换镜头、如何生成字幕，属于完成任务的方法；片头文件在哪里、字体用哪一款、横屏和竖屏分别怎样输出，属于项目资料和偏好；哪些片段不能删、成片交给谁确认，则属于具体工作要求。

模型升级可能改变第一部分。过去需要逐步讲解的方法，后来一句话就能可靠完成，旧的长说明便值得重新检查。后面几部分却不会仅因模型更强而自动获得答案。通用模型无法从一般知识中得知某个团队刚确认的片头版本。

因此，判断一个 Skill 是否过时，不能只看模型能否完成同类演示。更有用的比较是：去掉它之后，用户关心的哪些结果会发生变化？若变化只在过时的操作步骤，删减可能让流程更简单；若丢失的是项目规范，仍然需要一个可靠的保存位置。

## Skill 可以保存程序和资源

Anthropic 对 Agent Skills 的介绍把它定义为组织在目录中的指令、脚本和资源，并通过逐步加载减少无关内容进入上下文。这个设计说明，Skill 的载体比一段提示词更宽：它也可以把确定的计算交给脚本，把只有部分任务需要的资料放在单独文件里。

例如，假设每次输出都要遵守同一组文件命名规则，并生成几个固定尺寸的封面。把这些要求封装在可重复执行的程序中，就不必每次让模型重新发明处理方法。模型负责理解这次内容，程序负责执行已经明确的变换。

但打包在一起并不意味着一切都该自动运行。资源是否适用于当前项目、脚本依赖是否齐全、生成结果是否满足需求，仍需要检查。一个内容丰富的 Skill，也可能带着错误假设或已经失效的操作路径。

## 层层封装，容易藏住决定

当一个提示词要求安装多个 Skill，每个 Skill 又引用其他提示词时，最难找的往往不是入口，而是某条决定究竟来自哪里。

设想两套内容 Skill 都规定标题风格，一套要求克制，一套要求强烈吸引点击。单独使用时各有用途，一起加载却可能互相覆盖。再增加一层总提示词，未必能消除冲突，反而可能让使用者更难判断改哪份文件。

拆解这种复杂度，可以从所有权入手：通用制作方法保存在可复用能力里，项目偏好由项目资料管理，这次任务的例外写在任务要求中。每一层负责不同的信息，就不必把同一个字体、同一句标题规则复制到所有文件。

这是一种组织建议，并不是某种格式自带的保证。实际效果还取决于 Agent 能否找到正确资料，以及它如何处理相互矛盾的要求。

## 清理时，用旧任务做比较

模型更新之后，直接把所有 Skill 删除，或者永久保留所有历史补丁，都缺少依据。更稳妥的做法是挑几个经常发生的任务，在同一组输入上比较：完整 Skill、删掉通用步骤的精简版，以及不使用 Skill 的版本。

需要观察的结果也可以很具体：是否沿用正确素材，是否满足输出规格，哪里需要人重新提醒，完成后是否出现额外返工。这样的比较不能只看一次漂亮的样例；尤其是旧 Skill 曾经修复的失败，要重新放进去验证。

最终留下来的内容，可能越来越少讲模型本来就知道的常识，越来越多记录这项工作特有的事实和约束。Skill 是否值得保留，由它能否稳定传递这些信息来决定。文件叫 Prompt 还是 Skill，远没有其中保存了什么重要。

Can a single sentence already get a model to make a video? Does it still need a video-editing Skill installed? If all you want is a picture and sound, you might get a result quickly. But if you want to use your own subtitles, assets, pacing, and publishing specifications, the problem becomes much more specific.

A presentation about producing an AI news briefing showed another level of complexity: the user gives a prompt that asks a Bot to install four or five existing Skills, then calls on them to complete the task. An arrangement originally created to avoid repeating instructions gradually needs another layer of instructions before it can be used. The boundary between Prompts and Skills becomes blurred, but the things users want to preserve may not be the same.

## A model’s ability to do the work is one thing; knowing what you want requires another layer of information

Imagine a video-editing Skill as having several different parts. How to cut between shots and how to generate subtitles are methods for completing the task. Where the intro file is, which font to use, and how to export in landscape and portrait formats are project materials and preferences. Which clips must not be removed and who should approve the finished video are specific work requirements.

A model upgrade may change the first part. Methods that once needed step-by-step explanation may later work reliably with a single sentence, making the old, lengthy instructions worth reviewing. But the other parts do not come with answers just because the model has become stronger. A general-purpose model cannot learn from general knowledge which version of the intro a team has just approved.

So when deciding whether a Skill is outdated, don’t look only at whether the model can complete a similar demo. A more useful comparison is: without it, which results the user cares about would change? If the only changes involve outdated operating steps, trimming them may simplify the process. If what gets lost is the project specification, a reliable place to store it is still needed.

## A Skill can store procedures and resources

Anthropic’s introduction to Agent Skills defines them as instructions, scripts, and resources organized in directories, with progressive loading used to reduce irrelevant content in the context. This design shows that a Skill can be more than a prompt: it can also hand well-defined calculations to scripts and keep materials needed for only some tasks in separate files.

For example, suppose every output must follow the same file-naming rules and include covers in several fixed sizes. Encapsulating these requirements in a program that can be run repeatedly means the model does not have to reinvent the process every time. The model handles understanding the content for this task; the program carries out transformations that have already been specified.

But bundling things together does not mean they should all run automatically. Whether the resources apply to the current project, whether script dependencies are in place, and whether the generated result meets the requirements still need to be checked. A content-rich Skill can still contain incorrect assumptions or an operating path that no longer works.

## Layers of encapsulation can hide decisions

When one prompt asks for multiple Skills to be installed, and each Skill in turn references other prompts, the hardest thing to find is often not the entry point, but where a particular decision came from.

Imagine two content Skills that both set a headline style: one calls for restraint, the other for strong click appeal. Each may be useful on its own, but loading both can cause one to override the other. Adding another layer of master prompt may not resolve the conflict; it may instead make it harder for users to know which file to change.

One way to break down this complexity is to start with ownership: keep general production methods in reusable capabilities, manage project preferences in project materials, and put exceptions for the current task in its requirements. When each layer is responsible for different information, there is no need to copy the same font or headline rule into every file.

This is an organizational recommendation, not a guarantee that comes with any particular format. The actual results also depend on whether the Agent can find the right materials and how it handles conflicting requirements.

## When cleaning up, compare against old tasks

After a model update, deleting every Skill outright or keeping every historical patch forever both lack a solid basis. A more reliable approach is to pick several recurring tasks and compare versions using the same inputs: the full Skill, a streamlined version with the general steps removed, and a version that uses no Skill.

The results to observe can also be specific: whether the correct assets were used, whether the output specifications were met, where a person had to give a reminder, and whether extra rework was needed afterward. This comparison should not rely on a single polished example; in particular, failures that the old Skill once fixed should be included in the validation again.

The content that remains may spend less time on common knowledge that the model already has and more time recording facts and constraints specific to this work. Whether a Skill is worth keeping depends on whether it can reliably convey that information. What matters far more than whether the file is called a Prompt or a Skill is what it stores.

## 沿着一个后台任务读下去

以一个假设项目为例：用户上传文件后，系统把转换任务放进队列。先找到任务在哪里创建、谁消费它、结果保存到哪里，看看用户怎样知道处理结束。

读到这里，能确认的是调用和数据流向。为什么选后台执行，还要继续找资料。可能是任务耗时太长，可能是要限制并发，也可能来自已有基础设施。没有设计记录时，让模型把这些解释列成候选，并指出各自需要什么证据。

接着查失败路径。进程在保存结果前退出，任务会不会再跑一次？再跑会不会生成重复文件？如果模型说可以放心重试，就让它指出防止重复写入的代码。找不到时，这一项判断还不能成立。

这样读下来，一份宽泛的架构讲解会变成几个可以继续查证的问题。

## 改一个条件，看看方案还合不合适

假设这个转换任务原来每小时只有几次，现在每分钟几百次。先估计单次处理耗时与可用并发，再看队列会积压多久。若用户必须等结果才能继续操作，也需要重新考虑后台任务的反馈方式。

这些分析不一定要求重做整个系统。可以在实验项目中只验证最担心的一项，例如重复提交是否会产生重复记录。记录输入、观察结果，以及还没覆盖的情况，比只保存一句该架构可扩展更方便以后使用。

有时答案是现有方案已经够用。为了一个低频任务引入复杂队列，可能反而增加部署和排障负担。理解架构也包括知道什么时候可以少做一点。

## 记下这个决定当时解决了什么

Michael Nygard 提出的[架构决策记录](https://cognitect.com/blog/2011/11/15/documenting-architecture-decisions)，用短文保存重要决定的背景、状态和后果。Martin Fowler 的[说明](https://martinfowler.com/bliki/ArchitectureDecisionRecord.html)也建议保留旧决定，在被替代时链接到新的记录。

After reading an AI-organized project overview, you may know which framework, database, and queue it uses, yet still not know how to make those choices in your own project. This gap is common: technical names are easy to remember, but the conditions behind choosing them may not be written in the code.

The seventh episode introduced using REA to analyze a large project, then having a model explain the architecture and organize the documentation. With that overview in hand, you can investigate one specific decision instead of rushing to judge whether the whole architecture is good.

## Follow a Background Task Through the Code

Take a hypothetical project: after a user uploads a file, the system puts a conversion task in a queue. First find where the task is created, what consumes it, and where the result is saved. Then see how the user knows processing is complete.

At this point, you can confirm the calls and the direction of the data flow. To find out why background processing was chosen, you need to keep looking. Perhaps the task takes too long, perhaps concurrency needs to be limited, or perhaps the choice comes from existing infrastructure. If there is no design record, ask the model to list these explanations as candidates and point out what evidence each would require.

Next, inspect the failure path. If the process exits before saving the result, will the task run again? If it does, could it generate duplicate files? If the model says retries are safe, ask it to point to the code that prevents duplicate writes. If you cannot find it, that judgment is not yet established.

Read this way, a broad architecture explanation becomes a set of questions that can be investigated further.

## Change One Condition and See Whether the Approach Still Fits

Suppose this conversion task used to run only a few times per hour, but now runs hundreds of times per minute. First estimate the processing time per task and the available concurrency, then see how long the queue will build up. If users must wait for the result before continuing, you also need to reconsider how the background task communicates progress.

These analyses do not necessarily require rebuilding the whole system. In an experimental project, you can validate just the point you are most concerned about, such as whether duplicate submissions create duplicate records. Recording the input, the observed result, and the cases not yet covered is more useful later than saving only the statement “this architecture is scalable.”

Sometimes the answer is that the existing approach is already sufficient. Introducing a complex queue for an infrequent task may instead increase deployment and troubleshooting burdens. Understanding architecture also means knowing when you can do less.

## Record What the Decision Was Solving at the Time

Michael Nygard's [Architecture Decision Records](https://cognitect.com/blog/2011/11/15/documenting-architecture-decisions) preserve the context, status, and consequences of important decisions in short documents. Martin Fowler's [explanation](https://martinfowler.com/bliki/ArchitectureDecisionRecord.html) also recommends keeping old decisions and linking to a new record when they are superseded.

For the exercise above, a note could state how long file conversion usually takes, whether users can leave the page, why background processing was adopted, and how duplicate tasks are handled. If any item is only a guess, keep a “to check” marker and the relevant code location.

When a similar need comes up next time, compare these conditions first. If usage frequency, how long users wait, and the cost of failure are all different, the old approach can only provide a list of questions; it cannot be used directly as the answer.

一个 Skill 的名字带着作者前缀，使用者便能直接让 Agent 去仓库安装这一组工具。这个名字先承担检索和调用的功能，也顺带把作者带进了每一次使用。

相比一条很快滑走的动态，这种接触有可能反复发生。但名字出现得多，并不保证作者得到信任；作品被大量转发，也不保证有人愿意长期使用。免费开放作品之后，留下什么，比发布当天有多热闹更值得追踪。

## 名字让人找得到，作品让人有理由回来

统一前缀有一个直接好处：当多个 Skill 都叫写作、摘要或剪辑时，作者名可以帮助区分来源。它既方便人记忆，也方便在对话里描述要调用哪一套能力。

这样的辨识度仍需要实际体验支撑。第一次安装可能来自一段演示，第二次调用通常需要作品确实解决过问题。如果结果稳定、文档清楚、遇到问题能找到说明，作者名字就有机会成为一种选择线索。

反过来，前缀如果只是挤占界面、不断提醒用户关注，使用者记住的也可能是打扰。署名最好出现在自然的来源位置：仓库、安装入口、说明文档和版本记录。作品首先需要让人顺利完成事情。

## 从曝光到收入，中间有几次不同的选择

节目里讨论过用游戏、视频或 Skill 获得关注，再寻找商业机会的路径。这条路径存在吸引力，因为作品可以同时展示能力与想法。但其中每一步，都需要使用者做出新的选择。

看到演示，只能说明内容触达了人；打开仓库说明对作品有兴趣；成功运行说明跨过了使用门槛；以后还会回来，才逐渐形成持续关系。至于付费，还需要一个清楚的购买对象，例如托管、维护、定制或其他服务。

这些环节不能用同一个热度数字代替。GitHub 的仓库流量工具分别提供访问、克隆、来源站点和热门内容等信息，而且有观察窗口限制。即使拥有这些数据，克隆也不等于长期使用，更不能直接解释收入。它们适合帮助定位哪一步发生变化，而非给商业成功盖章。

对个人作者而言，一个比关注数更具体的问题可能是：最近来咨询的人，究竟是看过作品，还是已经用过作品？两种联系的需求、期待和后续服务，可能完全不同。

## 开源后仍然有人需要原作者

代码或 Skill 可以被复制，经验却未必随着一次下载完整转移。新的工具版本出现之后要不要调整，哪些用法曾经失败，什么情况下不该用，这些判断通常会在维护中继续积累。

原作者因此可以保留一条有用的持续关系：维护可运行的版本，解释设计选择，收集真实问题，再把改进返回作品。别人仍然可以做得更好，使用者也没有义务忠于原作者；留下来的理由，需要在之后的工作中持续成立。

这也意味着，开源的价值并不只剩流量。作品可以被团队复用，可以降低别人解决问题的成本，可以吸引贡献者，也可以让作者获得更具体的反馈。是否走向商业化，是其中一种选择，不是所有作品必须抵达的终点。

## 爆款故事缺少没有被看见的部分

一个作品走红的案例，能证明这条路径有人走通过，却无法说明大多数人照做会得到同样结果。没有走红的尝试、作者此前的积累、原有受众和持续投入，都可能没有出现在传播最广的版本里。

所以，把作品作为一次有限投入的试验，通常比把它当作必然成立的收入公式更诚实。先确定要服务的人、能完成的任务、愿意承担的维护范围，再观察是否出现真实使用。即使没有带来商业机会，作品本身也可能留下可复用能力和公开的工作样本。

如果关注突然增加，下一步也不一定是立刻再做一个爆款。修复安装问题、把常见问题写清楚、说明支持到什么程度，可能更有助于把一次围观变成下一次使用。

作者最终被记住的理由，可以从一个前缀开始，却需要由不断兑现的作品来延续。热度给人一次认识你的机会，之后是否再来，要靠新的使用经验回答。

When a Skill’s name carries an author prefix, users can ask an Agent to install that set of tools directly from the repository. The name first serves a search and invocation function, while also bringing the author into every use.

Compared with a post that quickly scrolls out of view, this kind of contact may happen repeatedly. But a name appearing often does not guarantee that the author earns trust; a work being widely shared does not guarantee that anyone is willing to use it over the long term. After making work freely available, what remains is more worth tracking than how much buzz there was on launch day.

## A name makes work findable; the work gives people a reason to return

A consistent prefix has one direct benefit: when multiple Skills are all called writing, summarization, or editing, the author’s name can help distinguish their sources. It makes them easier to remember and makes it easier to describe in a conversation which set of capabilities to invoke.

That kind of recognition still needs to be backed by real experience. The first install may come from a demo; the second invocation usually requires that the work has actually solved a problem. If the results are consistent, the documentation is clear, and users can find guidance when they run into trouble, the author’s name may become a cue for choosing it.

Conversely, if the prefix only takes up space in the interface and keeps reminding users to pay attention, they may remember it as an annoyance. Attribution is best placed where the source naturally belongs: the repository, installation entry point, documentation, and version history. First and foremost, the work needs to help people get things done smoothly.

## From exposure to income, there are several different choices in between

The show discussed a path of using games, videos, or Skills to attract attention and then looking for commercial opportunities. This path is appealing because a work can showcase both capabilities and ideas. But at every step, users need to make a new choice.

Seeing a demo only shows that the content reached people; opening the repository shows interest in the work; successfully running it shows that they crossed the usage barrier; only when they come back later does an ongoing relationship gradually take shape. As for payment, there also needs to be a clear offering to buy, such as hosting, maintenance, customization, or another service.

These stages cannot be represented by the same popularity number. GitHub’s repository traffic tools provide separate information about visits, clones, referring sites, and popular content, and they have limits on the observation window. Even with this data, a clone does not mean long-term use, much less explain revenue directly. These metrics can help pinpoint where something changed; they cannot certify commercial success.

For an individual author, a more concrete question than follower count might be: Were the people who recently got in touch drawn by seeing the work, or have they already used it? The needs, expectations, and follow-up services associated with those two kinds of contact may be completely different.

## People still need the original author after open-sourcing

Code or a Skill can be copied, but experience does not necessarily transfer in full with a single download. After new versions of tools appear, whether to make adjustments, which approaches have failed, and when not to use them are judgments that usually continue to build through maintenance.

The original author can therefore maintain a useful, ongoing relationship: keep a working version maintained, explain design choices, collect real problems, and feed improvements back into the work. Others may still do it better, and users are under no obligation to stay loyal to the original author; the reason to stick around needs to keep holding up through the work that follows.

This also means that open source is not just about traffic. A work can be reused by teams, lower the cost for others to solve problems, attract contributors, and give the author more specific feedback. Commercialization is one possible choice, not a destination every work must reach.

## The parts missing from a breakout success story

A case of a work taking off can prove that someone has made this path work, but it cannot show that most people who follow suit will get the same result. Attempts that did not take off, the author’s prior experience, existing audience, and sustained effort may all be absent from the version that spreads the furthest.

So it is usually more honest to treat a work as a limited-investment experiment than as a guaranteed formula for income. First define whom it will serve, what task it can complete, and what scope of maintenance you are willing to take on, then see whether real use emerges. Even if it does not bring commercial opportunities, the work itself may still leave behind reusable capabilities and a public work sample.

If attention suddenly increases, the next step does not necessarily have to be making another breakout hit right away. Fixing installation problems, clarifying common questions, and explaining the level of support available may do more to turn a one-time look into another use.

The reason an author is ultimately remembered may start with a prefix, but it takes work that continues to deliver to sustain that recognition. Buzz gives people one chance to learn about you; whether they come back depends on the experience of using what you make next.

帮一个人安排生活，听起来是 Agent 很自然的用途。可当任务涉及购买、预约、账户和售后时，一句自然语言背后很快就连着多个系统。模型知道应该做什么，只是开始；它还需要能够读取信息、发起操作，并确认结果。

门店经营则提供了另一种起点。订单、评价、营销活动这些事情每天发生，经营者知道哪里费时间，也更容易指出一份报告是否漏掉了问题。第 006 期对个人助理的讨论，最终转向了美团等平台的商家工具。这个转向值得解释，但不能直接推出国内只有商家 Agent 能成立。

## 商家任务自带一部分上下文

一个陌生的个人用户说帮我安排明天，系统可能还不知道他的工作时间、家庭分工、预算与偏好。相比之下，门店经营任务可以从较窄的问题开始：汇总昨日评价，找出重复出现的投诉，列出需要店长查看的订单异常。

范围较窄并不意味着技术上一定简单，而是业务对象更容易指认。哪家店、哪段时间、哪一组数据、交给谁看，往往可以在现有工作流程中找到答案。用户也能用已有经验判断结果是否相关。

美团官网刊载的 CatPaw 介绍，把数据汇总、异常识别和经营建议列为商家场景，并强调价格等关键决定仍由经营者作出。这是平台对产品用途的说明，不是独立测得的收益数据。它展示了一种务实的边界：先把分散信息整理到经营者可以判断的程度。

## 接近业务，不等于自动拥有权限

平台服务过大量商家，可以积累对业务流程的理解；某个 Agent 能否使用某家店的数据，仍取决于实际授权和接入。不能因为属于同一个生态，就假设所有账户、订单与操作都能随意调用。

可以用三个问题检查一个落地方案。它能看到完成任务所需的数据吗？它有执行相应操作的入口吗？操作后能否查到结果？这三个问题分别对应信息、动作和反馈，缺少任何一项，都可能停留在给建议的层面。

假设系统能分析差评，却不能修改商品说明，它仍可作为经营助手发挥作用，只是交付物应当是待处理事项，而不能宣称已经改善了商品页面。能力范围说得准确，才便于人接手剩余工作。

这个判断也适用于个人助理。获取旅行建议与完成一笔可查询的预订，是不同的服务深度。模型能力相近的两个产品，可能因为可用接口不同，表现出完全不同的实际用途。

## 消费者服务提供了反例

阿里巴巴对千问 App 的官方介绍，明确列出了通过淘宝即时零售下单，并在对话中完成支付的消费者场景。无论具体体验是否稳定，这至少说明个人消费任务也在产品的落地范围内，不能把它们概括为没有用武之地。

值得注意的是这些能力接入了已有的商品、交易与支付系统。它们与商家工具共享的条件，是能把意图交给实际业务处理。用户身份一端是消费者，另一端是经营者，并不改变这个基本要求。

因此，比国内外或个人与商家的简单二分更值得研究的，是服务可以深入到哪里。一个平台可以先覆盖自身能提供完整操作路径的任务，独立助理则需要通过授权接口、合作或界面操作接入更多服务。各条路径的成本与可靠性，需要放到具体任务里比较。

## 商业价值更清楚，也更容易被追问

商家场景的吸引力还在于，使用者通常能说出问题造成的损失：重复整理花了多少时间，哪些异常经常漏看，报告出来后谁来处理。这给产品提供了较明确的评估方向。

不过，报告更快并不自动等于经营更好。减少整理时间、改善决策、增加收入是不同层次的结果。若缺少后续记录，最多只能确认前一层，不能把收入变化都归因于 Agent。

个人助理也有类似问题，只是价值未必都以收入衡量。方便、安心或完成原本搁置的事务，都可能成立。商家任务的优势在于边界和反馈往往更明确，并非个人生活不值得服务。

当 Agent 先进入门店或电商后台，可以把它理解为对现有业务条件的利用。真正决定它能走多远的，仍是可获得的信息、可执行的动作，以及结果能否回到使用者手中。

Helping someone organize their life sounds like a natural use for an Agent. But when a task involves purchases, appointments, accounts, and after-sales service, a single natural-language request quickly connects to multiple systems. Knowing what to do is only the beginning for a model; it also needs to be able to read information, initiate actions, and confirm the results.

Store operations offer another starting point. Orders, reviews, and marketing campaigns happen every day. Operators know what takes time and can more easily point out whether a report has missed a problem. The discussion of personal assistants in episode 006 eventually turned to merchant tools on platforms such as Meituan. That shift is worth explaining, but it does not justify concluding that only merchant Agents can succeed in China.

## Merchant tasks come with some of their own context

When an unfamiliar user says, “Help me plan tomorrow,” the system may not know their work schedule, family responsibilities, budget, or preferences. By comparison, store operations can start with a narrower question: summarize yesterday’s reviews, find recurring complaints, or list order anomalies that the store manager should look at.

A narrower scope does not necessarily make a task technically simple. It does make the business objects easier to identify. Which store, what time period, which data, and who should see it can often be determined from existing workflows. Users can also draw on their experience to judge whether the result is relevant.

Meituan’s official website describes CatPaw as handling data summaries, anomaly detection, and operational recommendations for merchants, while emphasizing that key decisions such as pricing remain with the operator. This is the platform’s description of the product’s intended use, not independently measured data on its benefits. It illustrates a pragmatic boundary: first organize scattered information into a form that operators can assess.

## Being close to the business does not mean automatically having permission

A platform that serves many merchants can build up an understanding of business workflows. Whether a particular Agent can use a particular store’s data still depends on actual authorization and integration. Being part of the same ecosystem is no reason to assume that every account, order, and operation can be accessed freely.

You can assess a deployment plan with three questions. Can it see the data needed to complete the task? Does it have an entry point for carrying out the relevant action? Can the result be checked afterward? These questions correspond to information, action, and feedback. Missing any one of them may leave the system at the level of offering suggestions.

Suppose a system can analyze negative reviews but cannot edit product descriptions. It can still serve as an operational assistant, but its deliverable should be a list of items to address; it should not claim to have improved the product page. Describing the scope of its capabilities accurately makes it easier for a person to take over the remaining work.

The same applies to personal assistants. Getting travel recommendations and completing a booking whose status can be checked are different levels of service. Two products with similar model capabilities may have entirely different practical uses because they have access to different interfaces.

## Consumer services offer a counterexample

Alibaba’s official introduction to the Qwen App explicitly lists consumer scenarios such as placing an order through Taobao’s instant retail service and completing payment in the conversation. Whether the experience is consistently reliable or not, this shows at least that personal shopping tasks are within the product’s deployment scope. They cannot be summed up as having no useful role.

It is worth noting that these capabilities connect to existing product, transaction, and payment systems. What they share with merchant tools is the ability to hand an intention off to actual business processes. Whether the user is a consumer or an operator does not change this basic requirement.

So the more useful question is how far a service can go, rather than a simple division between China and other countries or between individuals and merchants. A platform can first cover tasks for which it can provide a complete action path. An independent assistant needs to connect to more services through authorized interfaces, partnerships, or interaction with user interfaces. The costs and reliability of these approaches need to be compared for specific tasks.

## Business value is clearer, and easier to question

Another appeal of merchant scenarios is that users can often describe the losses caused by a problem: how much time repeated organization takes, which anomalies are often missed, and who will act on a report once it is ready. This gives the product a relatively clear direction for evaluation.

However, a faster report does not automatically mean better business performance. Reducing time spent organizing information, improving decisions, and increasing revenue are outcomes at different levels. Without follow-up records, at most you can confirm the first; you cannot attribute all changes in revenue to the Agent.

Personal assistants face a similar issue, though their value is not necessarily measured in revenue. Convenience, peace of mind, or completing a task that had been put off can all count. Merchant tasks have the advantage that their boundaries and feedback are often clearer; that does not mean people’s personal lives are not worth serving.

When an Agent first enters a store or an e-commerce merchant console, this can be understood as making use of existing business conditions. What ultimately determines how far it can go is still the information it can access, the actions it can perform, and whether the results can get back to the user.

一个任务看起来很适合交给 AI 团队：抓取 GitHub Trending 和 Product Hunt 的热榜，整理成内容，再接上语音合成，做成持续播放的播客。

几个 Bot 很快商量出方案。分工明确，彼此通知修改，版本不断增加。旁观这场讨论，会觉得工作已经有条不紊地推进；真正等到执行，却发现耗时很长，Token 也消耗得很快。这是一次使用中的观察，材料没有给出完整耗时和账单，但它足以提出一个问题：群里越来越热闹时，离成品究竟更近了多少？

## 给角色起名字，比划清任务容易

把技术、产品、营销角色拉进同一个群，很容易获得组织起来的感觉。每个角色都有立场，能够补充意见，也能对其他人的方案提出异议。在产品脑暴里，这种互动确实可能帮助使用者发现自己没有想到的角度。

不过，角色的差异不自动变成执行上的独立性。一个营销 Bot 可以评价标题，一个产品 Bot 也可以评价标题，第三个 Bot 再总结双方意见。如果没有人拥有定稿权，意见越多，标题越难结束。

热榜播客的工作可以按对象拆分：两路信息分别采集，编辑负责选题和脚本，语音环节接收定稿。这样的划分提供了输入和输出的边界。按照职位搭一套组织，则可能让每个角色都参与每个环节，工作从制作内容变成持续讨论如何制作内容。

判断分工是否有效，可以先问一个具体问题：某个 Bot 交回什么东西之后，这一步就算结束？如果答案仍是参与讨论，任务就没有真正被分出去。

## 并行收益取决于任务之间要等多少次

两路热榜采集可以同时开始；配音需要等待脚本，最终混音又要等待音频。增加执行者，能够缩短独立工作的等待，却无法消除本来就存在的前后依赖。

更麻烦的是人为增加的依赖。假设脚本写完后，五个角色必须逐一同意才能进入配音，那么系统就多出五次沟通机会。任何一次提出新要求，都可能把前面的工作重新打开。这里描述的是一种可能的设计，并不是对那次试验内部实现的断言。

Anthropic 在 2025 年公布的多 Agent 研究系统经验里，也把可并行性作为重要条件：独立方向的广泛检索适合分给子 Agent；大量共享上下文、相互依赖的任务则更难受益。该团队报告，多 Agent 系统在其数据中约消耗普通聊天十五倍的 Token。比较基准是聊天，并非所有单 Agent 工作流；这个数字不能直接套到任何产品账单上。

这份经验支持的判断很有限，也很实用：多 Agent 能购买更多探索容量，但需要足够有价值、可以独立展开的工作来消化它。

## 脑暴和交付可以采用不同的组织方式

脑暴阶段不必急着消灭所有重复。让几个角色分别挑毛病，有时就是为了延迟收敛，找出被忽略的可能性。使用者从不同视角里获得灵感，也是这一阶段可以接受的结果。

进入交付阶段后，目标变了。谁决定采用哪版方案，谁可以修改已确认的要求，哪些问题需要退回用户，都应该收紧。继续保留一个人人都能随时改方向的群聊，会把探索阶段的开放性带进本应执行的阶段。

一个可尝试的安排是让讨论有终点：先收集若干不同方案，再由明确的负责人定稿；后续执行者可以报告阻碍，但不因个人偏好重开全部讨论。这样的安排仍然允许分工，只是让分工围绕产物推进。

## 管理一支 AI 团队的快乐，也可以单独成立

角色扮演的乐趣无需伪装成生产力。看不同性格的 Bot 讨论产品、接住一个突然冒出的点子，本身可以是一种娱乐和创作体验。只要使用者愿意为此付出时间与费用，它就有自己的价值。

容易混淆的地方，是把团队的存在感当成交付能力。头像多、发言密、方案整齐，都不足以说明任务完成得更好。若目标是做出一档播客，值得比较的是相同要求下，成品质量、等待时间、费用和人工介入次数如何变化。

组织结构可以很轻。只有在某一块工作值得独立展开、结果可以清楚交接时，再增加一个执行者。让一个 Bot 留在前台回应用户、另一个在后台处理长任务，也是一种明确的分工；它的价值不需要靠一场全员会议证明。
